Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: issue #6304, a spaced numeric refspec is dropped as a file-descriptor number

Planning ref: `HEAD` = `e82e1ff8cf0da58b93a43ccbbaf2456cfa6895d1`, branch `claude/sync-pr-merge-guard-twin`. This matches the issue's integration branch, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `_shell_segments_with_operators`
Scope-mode justification: The finding sits in one helper, `_shell_segments_with_operators` in `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` (lines 249–282). At line 268, any all-digit token just before a `<`/`>` operator is popped. `shlex` gives `['git','push','origin','2','>','/dev/null']` for both `2>/dev/null` and `2 > /dev/null`, so the helper cannot tell them apart. In Bash only the first one is an fd redirection; the second pushes branch `2`. The fix stays inside that helper. It reads the lexer's stream offset to decide whether the digits were unquoted and touching the operator. In every other case, including spaced, quoted or unclear forms, the token stays an argument, so the push parser checks branch `2` (fail closed). The twin copy under `workflow-templates/` must stay byte-identical, which `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1022` enforces, so it gets the same edit. Per the Boil the Lake rule (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete adjacency-and-quoting check costs only a few lines more than a spaced-only check, so the plan does the complete one. No new dependency or interface.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: fix `_shell_segments_with_operators` and add `import io`.
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: same edit, byte-identical.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: new parametrized cases.
- `changelog.d/6304-pr-merge-guard-spaced-numeric-refspec.md`: new changelog fragment (CLAUDE.md §20), `<!-- changelog: security -->`.

No workflow, script-staging, or `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS` changes. The hook is a `.claude/` asset and reaches consumers on the `@stable` sync.

### 2. Functions to change
`_shell_segments_with_operators(command)` (`.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:249`):
- Build the lexer over `io.StringIO(command)` instead of the raw string. Keep `posix=True`, `punctuation_chars=_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS`, `commenters=""`, `whitespace=" \t\r"` and `whitespace_split=True` exactly as they are.
- Drive the lexer with `get_token()` until `lexer.eof` instead of `for token in lexer`. For each token, record `start` (the stream's `tell()` before the read) and `end` (`tell()` after).
- Keep the start and end of the last plain segment token (`last_word_span`).
- When a redirect-operator token arrives (`<`, `>`, `>>`, `>&`, `<&`, `&>`, and so on, as the existing `set(token) <= set("<>") | {"&"}` test detects), pop `segment[-1]` only if all of these hold:
  - `segment` is non-empty and `segment[-1]` was the token just before the operator;
  - in the raw text, the character at `prev_end - 1` is the operator's first character (`<` or `>`). This works because, when an operator touches a word, `shlex` reads the operator character and pushes it back, so `tell()` sits one character past the word. When whitespace separates them, that character is whitespace;
  - the raw slice `command[prev_start:prev_end - 1]`, with leading `" \t\r"` stripped, fully matches `[0-9]+`. That means the word was unquoted digits. A quoted `"2">x` is an argument in Bash, not an fd.
- Otherwise leave the token in `segment`, so `_push_targets` sees it as a refspec and `_branch_ref("2")` sends branch `2` through the merged-PR check.
- Add a short comment explaining that Bash treats only unquoted digits immediately before `<`/`>` as an fd (IO_NUMBER), and that every other case is kept as an argument so the guard fails closed.
- The redirect-target skip (`redirect_target`) and the segmenting logic stay unchanged. A `ValueError` from `shlex` still reaches `_guarded_git_invocations`, which already catches it.

No other function changes. `_shell_segments` (callers at lines 573 and 639) does not strip fd digits and is out of scope.

### 3. Data structures affected
None. The return shape (`list[tuple[str, list[str]]]`) is unchanged.

### 4. API / interface changes
None. CLI, hook payload, exit codes and messages are unchanged. Behaviour change: spaced or quoted numeric words before a redirect are now treated as push arguments.

## Decisions
### D1 — Use stream offsets for adjacency instead of a second tokenizer
- Chosen: wrap the command in `io.StringIO` and compare `tell()` offsets against the raw command text.
- Alternatives considered: read `shlex`'s private `_pushback_chars`; run a regex pre-scan over the raw command; write a custom Bash tokenizer.
- Why: offsets use only the public `tell()` on our own stream, and they also let us check that the word was unquoted. A regex cannot follow quoting reliably, and a new tokenizer would be a large change to a security hook.

### D2 — Unclear tokens stay positional
- Chosen: drop a digit token only when it is proven to be an adjacent, unquoted fd number; otherwise keep it.
- Alternatives considered: return an "uncertain" target with a warning for every digit token next to a redirect.
- Why: keeping the token makes `_push_targets` check the named branch. That matches Bash, and an unparsable ref still falls back to `_branch_ref` returning `None`, which checks the current branch. This is the fail-closed behaviour the recommendation asks for, without new prompts for ordinary `2>&1` usage.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: the hook parses an untrusted Bash command from the agent session before it runs. The parser decides which branches get the merged-PR check, so treating an argument as an fd lets a push skip the guard (Tampering).
- Authorization: no new surface. The hook still checks every resolved push destination.
- Input validation: a word is dropped only when it is unquoted, all digits and touching a redirect operator. Spaced (`2 > x`), multi-space (`2  >x`), tab-separated and quoted (`"2">x`, `'2'>x`) forms stay arguments.
- Abuse cases covered:
  - `git push origin 2 > /dev/null` from a default-branch checkout targets branch `2`;
  - `git push origin x 2 >&1` pushes branches `x` and `2`;
  - `git push origin "2">/dev/null` pushes branch `2`.
- No secrets, logging, money state or GitHub API calls are involved.

### Risks and edge cases
- `git push origin 2>/dev/null` and `HEAD:feature/x 2>&1` must keep their current meaning, where the digit is an fd. The existing parametrized test at `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:929-930` pins this.
- Multi-digit fds (`10>x`, `12<in`) keep being dropped, as before.
- A redirect at the start of a segment (`> f git push …`) has no previous token; the existing `if segment` guard still applies.
- Bash's `{var}>x` form keeps today's behaviour: the token reaches `_branch_ref`, which returns `None` and checks the current branch.
- `\n` is a punctuation character, not whitespace. Offsets still work because newlines produce separate operator tokens.
- Twin drift: both files must be edited identically, or `test_…` at line 1022 fails.

### Testing considerations
- Add a parametrized test next to `test_push_parser_guards_real_destination` (around line 932). It uses the same `query_pull_requests` monkeypatch, where `MERGED_PR` is returned for branch `2`. It asserts `code == 2` and `"2" in lookups` for:
  - `git push origin 2 > /dev/null`
  - `git push origin 2  >/dev/null`
  - `git push origin "2">/dev/null`
  - `git push origin feature/open 2 >&1`
- Add a unit test of `guard._shell_segments_with_operators` that checks tokens directly:
  - `git push origin 2>/dev/null` gives `['git','push','origin']`;
  - `git push origin 2 > /dev/null` gives `['git','push','origin','2']`;
  - `x 12<in` gives `['x']`;
  - `x '2'>f` gives `['x','2']`.
- Existing cases must stay green: lines 924–931 and the twin byte-identity test at line 1022.
- Run: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py -q`, then `ruff check` on both hook copies.

### Pre-execution self-check
- Every cited path, function and line was read on this ref: guard lines 225–505, test lines 23–24, 915–965 and 1022.
- The tokenizer behaviour was checked on this runner. Adjacent `2>` gives `tell()` = 18 with `>` at index 17; spaced `2 >` gives `tell()` = 18 with a space at index 17; quoted `"2">` gives the raw slice `"2"`, which is rejected.
- `io` is not imported yet (imports at lines 81–95), so the plan adds it.
- No §20 automation, scheduler, supervisor or DB work is involved. The change only edits existing code in a Claude hook, which runs per tool call in interactive sessions. No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry is needed.
- PR body should use `Refs #3576`, since that is the security-audit tracker, and may use `Fixes #6304`.
